overall.summary: All fourteen tools implement their described core functions, and the divergences are edge-case behaviors: edit_file applies whitespace-tolerant matching despite the 'must match exactly' schema text, read_text_file decodes only utf-8 despite claiming to handle various encodings, and several tools have undocumented limits (100,000-entry walk cap, 15-second readdir timeout) and output extras (size summary footer, preserved inode/permissions on overwrite). At startup the server additionally resolves symlinks, prunes inaccessible directories, exits when none are usable, and can replace its entire allow-list at runtime from client-provided roots.

startup.behaviour: Resolves symlinks of command-line allowed directories at startup (realpath) and keeps both the advertised and resolved spellings for later path matching.
Warns on stderr and drops allowed directories that are missing or not directories; exits the process with code 1 if every specified directory is inaccessible.
Prints usage notes and 'Secure MCP Filesystem Server running on stdio' to stderr; sets process.exitCode = 1 when the stdio transport fails.
Reads the package's package.json at startup to determine the server version reported in serverInfo.

On 2025-era connections, after initialize the server requests roots from the client (roots/list) and replaces its allowed directories with the validated roots; every roots/list_changed notification re-fetches and replaces them, and a client withdrawing all roots revokes all access.
startup.evidence: dist/server.js: createServer (oninitialized, initialize, setNotificationHandler for notifications/roots/list_changed)

startup.behaviour: Exits the process with code 1 when it cannot operate (no command-line directories and a client that cannot provide roots); on 2026-07-28 connections started with no directories, every tool call returns an error instead of operating.
startup.evidence: dist/index.js: main (onCannotOperate); dist/server.js: initialize and the registerTool wrapper

undocumented_behaviours.behaviour: The walk stops with an error after 100,000 visited entries (WalkLimitError), and any readdir that takes over 15 seconds fails the whole call (FsTimeoutError).
undocumented_behaviours.evidence: dist/lib.js: createEntryBudget, readdirWithTimeout; dist/server.js: directory_tree handler

undocumented_behaviours.behaviour: An excludePattern without wildcards matches a name anywhere below the root (via **/ prefix), not only exact relative paths.
A symlink inside the tree that points outside the allowed directories fails the entire call rather than being skipped.
undocumented_behaviours.evidence: dist/server.js: directory_tree handler (validatePath at the start of buildTree)

undocumented_behaviours.behaviour: When oldText does not match exactly, the edit still succeeds via whitespace-tolerant line matching (trimmed line comparison) and the replacement lines are reindented to the file's indentation, despite the schema stating oldText 'must match exactly'.
The file's predominant line ending is preserved: a CRLF file is written back with CRLF endings.
All edits are applied in memory and the file is written only if every edit matches; a failing edit leaves the file completely unchanged.
The write goes through overwriteInPlace, so the file's inode, creation time, hard links and permission bits are preserved.
Uses fs.stat, which follows symlinks, so the reported metadata describes the link target rather than the link itself.
The returned list can change at runtime: on 2025-era connections the client's roots replace the command-line directories, and a client withdrawing all roots empties the list entirely.
Each directory may appear twice in the list: the advertised spelling and its realpath-resolved spelling.
Appends a summary footer (total file/directory counts and combined size) that the description does not mention.
Symlinks whose targets lie outside the allowed directories are listed with size 0 and an epoch mtime rather than being followed.
undocumented_behaviours.evidence: dist/server.js: list_directory_with_sizes handler (per-entry validatePath, catch returns size 0)

undocumented_behaviours.behaviour: Sorting by size is descending.
When source and destination are on different devices, the move copies the file (preserving mode and timestamps) and then removes the source, so the moved file gets a new inode.
undocumented_behaviours.evidence: dist/lib.js: moveFile (EXDEV fallback); dist/pinned-directory.js: moveFileAcrossDevices, copyIntoNewFile, keepModeAndTimes

undocumented_behaviours.behaviour: Directories cannot be moved across devices; the call fails with an error.
A failed cross-device move removes the partial copy and leaves the source file in place.
Returns an error when both head and tail are given: 'Cannot specify both head and tail parameters simultaneously'.
head/tail normalize line endings (CRLF is converted to LF; tail strips one trailing newline), so the returned text differs from the raw file bytes.
The MIME type is chosen solely from the file extension via a fixed map; any other extension is reported as application/octet-stream.
The entire file is buffered in memory and base64-encoded before being returned.

read_text_file.declared_effect_not_implemented: The description claims it 'Handles various text encodings', but the implementation reads only as utf-8 (dist/lib.js: readFileContent).

undocumented_behaviours.behaviour: Returns an error when both head and tail are given: 'Cannot specify both head and tail parameters simultaneously'.
head/tail normalize line endings (CRLF is converted to LF; tail strips one trailing newline), so the returned text differs from the raw file bytes.
Entries that fail validation (e.g. symlinks pointing outside the allowed directories) are silently skipped.
The walk stops with an error after 100,000 visited entries or a 15-second readdir stall, rather than returning partial results.
Overwriting writes in place through the existing file, preserving its inode, creation time, hard links and permission bits, rather than replacing the file.
The write is not crash-atomic: a crash mid-write can leave a partially written file.
Refuses to write through a symlink: an existing symlink at the target path fails with an error instead of writing to its target.
